name: Sweet potatoes
tile_uses: Rice bowls, tacos, beside anything roasted
why_now: Most of California's sweet potatoes come out of the ground around Merced in September and October. The new crop is on the shelves now — at its cheapest, and not yet tired from months in storage.
how_to_choose: Firm all over, with no soft ends
Medium and even in shape, so they cook at one speed
buy_this_much: 2 lbs. They keep, so they're the thing you cook the week it gets away from you.
price_note: Cheapest of the year through November, when the holidays push the price back up.

flavor_paths.name: Cut side down
flavor_paths.description: Halved, oiled, face down at 425°F. The crust is the point.

flavor_paths.name: Cubed and charred
flavor_paths.description: Small cubes, hot oven, for tacos and bowls.

flavor_paths.name: With the jar
flavor_paths.description: Split open, salsa macha spooned into the middle.

weekday_uses: Cubed and roasted into tacos with poblano
In a rice bowl with ground beef and pomegranate
Split open with yogurt, salt, and salsa macha
Cut side down beside pork chops
weekend_use: A whole tray, halved and roasted cut side down, on the table next to the braise.
storage: Somewhere cool and dark, not the fridge — cold turns the center hard and odd-tasting. They keep for weeks.
one_thing_to_learn: Cut side down is the whole trick. The flat face sits on the hot pan, the sugars caramelize into a dark crust, and the inside steams in its own skin. Flip it halfway and you lose the crust. Leave it alone for thirty-five minutes.
